title: Telemetry Baker: experiments and recipes for metrics, traces, dashboards
content:
Purpose:
This doc is an operational lab notebook — a set of lightweight experiments and concrete 'recipes' for shaping the telemetry we surface for inference. The metaphor: treat signals like baking — small controlled experiments, iterate on ingredient proportions, measure rise and flavor (signal fidelity). Goal: reduce dashboard noise, keep trace costs bounded, and preserve fast operator triage for token-serving incidents.

Quick context / problem statement:
- Observability panels are overloaded with high-cardinality dimensions and traces that blow budget.
- Operators need a fast ‘first look’ that points to candidate causes within 60–90s.
- We want decisions that are reversible and cheap to A/B test (i.e., toggles, sampling rates, lightweight enrichments).

Experiment matrix (recipe list):
1) Session-summary metric (compact):
   - ingredient: aggregate per-request summary at ingestion point (tokens_in, tokens_out, kv_hits, model_variant, routing_tier)
   - definition: one line per RPC representing compact fields; emitted at completion, 1 row per request; TTL 30d
   - intended use: fast cohort SLI slicing without reconstructing spans
   - risk: increased ingestion QPS; mitigations: only emit when request_duration > p90 or kv_miss=true (sampling hybrid)

2) Span condensation (tracing compression):
   - ingredient: collapse fanout spans (model->quantization->kv) into single condensed span when non-error and latency < 95th percentile
   - output: condensed span with annotations: condensed_duration_ms, condensed_token_count, condensed_path_tags
   - benefit: reduces stored span count and preserves essential anchors for debugging

3) Lightweight prompt-attribution anchor (enrichment):
   - ingredient: include 8-char prompt-hash and a prompt-trace-token that links metric row -> sampled verbose trace
   - policy: always include hash; include verbose prompt text only on sampled traces (1/1000) or when error codes present
   - reason: cheap attribution for correlation queries without leaking content at scale

4) Tiered trace-sampling budgeted plan:
   - baseline: 0.5% global sampling for verbose traces
   - escalation: 5% sample for requests that cross 'suspicion' heuristics (latency>p99, kv_miss and long tail tokens, model_fanout>1)
   - fallback retention: store condensed spans for all requests for 7d, verbose traces 30d for sampled set

Metrics definitions (compact canonical forms):
- request.count: delta counter, labels: tenant_id, model_family, route, routing_tier
- token.out.count: cumulative tokens emitted, labels: tenant_id, model_name, quantization_profile
- request.latency.ms.p50/p90/p99: histogram buckets, labels: model_name, region
- kv.cache.hit_rate: gauge (computed from kv_hit / kv_lookup), labels: shard, model_family
- condensed_span.count: counts of condensed spans emitted per minute, labels: reason=(normal|suspicion|error)

Dashboard smoke-test checklist (what to verify after a change):
- Panel latency queries finish within 2s for 90% queries (test on staging with scaled synthetic traffic)
- Top-10 tenant slicing works without exploding cardinality in UI; fallback to pre-aggregated lane if needed
- Time-to-first-action: from alert -> trace anchor link <= 60s (link must open to condensed span)
- Cost delta check: new trace/metric must not increase monthly bill for ingestion by more than 2% in baseline tests

Operator-first UX anchors (what to show at glance):
- Small summary card: requests/min, p95 latency, kv_warmth_index (0–1), condensed-error-rate
- Drill path: summary card -> top offending tenant/model -> condensed-span list -> sampled verbose trace link

Trace enrichment key list (what minimal keys to include):
- request_id (short uuid), prompt_hash (8c), model_variant, route, tenant_bucket, condensed_reason, kv_hits, kv_lookups, token_count_out, serve_node_id

Privacy and PII guardrails:
- Never include raw prompt text in non-sampled traces; sampled verbose traces only stored if prompt contains no detected PII (use PII-detector pipeline boolean)
- Prompt-hash is non-reversible; store mapping only in ephemeral investigation session logs (30m TTL)

Cost/volume estimates (back-of-envelope):
- Baseline requests: 120k/min (prod), condensed span size ~ 400 bytes -> 3.1 GB/day
- Verbose trace sampling at 0.5% -> estimated 25 MB/day (perk: low)
- Metric ingestion from session-summary rows (if emitted for 10% of requests) -> additional 360k rows/min, plan to route to pre-aggregation stream

Feature toggle plan (safe rollout):
- Feature flags: condensed-spans (boolean), prompt-hash (boolean), session-summary (enum: off/full/heuristic-sampled), verbose-trace-sampling-rate (number)
- Roll steps: dev -> internal-staging (1%) -> department beta (5%) -> org-wide (100%) with metric cost gates and rollback on cost/latency regressions

Open questions / notes-to-self:
- How to best incorporate tenant-weighted sampling so low-volume tenants get meaningful traces without blowing budget? (idea: reservoir per-tenant until cap)
- Should condensed spans be the canonical link target for alerts? Pros: cheap; cons: might miss context from children spans. Hybrid suggestion: condensed -> link to most recent verbose sample if exists
- Verify retention and GDPR export requirements for prompt-hash mapping table (legal).

Next short-term tasks (owners assigned):
- Diego: implement condensed-span emitter prototype (Q3 sprint)
- Priya: build sampling-budget simulator (quick script) and run against last-30d traffic (due 2025-07-05)
- Ethan: mock dashboard panels and run smoke-tests with synthetic traffic (due 2025-07-12)

Notes to self (style):
- Keep iterations small. Avoid additions that increase cardinality especially on tenant_id and prompt attributes.
- Preface any telemetry change with an expected-cost delta and a rollback toggle.

End of notebook entry.

Unresolved: long-term plan for model variant lineage tracing (how much lineage to carry without cardinality explosion).
